title: Jason Blum and James Wan Discuss Why Horror Is Hollywood’s Hottest Genre and How ‘Obsession’ Hit Big at Blumhouse Atomic’s Business of Fear
content:
ByJack Dunn

Blumhouse AtomicbossesJason BlumandJames Wantook a victory lap Wednesday at their Business of Fear panel, during which they discussed horror’s banner year at the box office and why “Obsession” became the breakout hit of the summer.

But before the horror talk began, they had to address the name change. Blum’s Blumhouse and Wan’s Atomic Monster merged in 2024, and the combined labels were therefore known as Blumhouse Atomic Monster. Recently,in early November, Blumhouse Atomic Monster rebranded to just Blumhouse Atomic. Blum explained they rebranded to give a more definitive identity to the overarching banner of the two companies, while also clearing the way for both distinct labels to take credit for their work.

Wan added that Blumhouse Atomic Monster was also “a bit of a mouthful.”

“As Jason pointed out, it really still is Blumhouse movies and Atomic Monster movies,” Wan added. “We’re still making the movies as one company, but still under two labels. We put out a bunch of movies, and so we have to sort of divide it. Some movies play better at Atomic Monster, some movies play better at Blumhouse. At the start of movies, even though it’s going to say Blumhouse Atomic Presents, our logos will still stand individually.”

It was then on to horror’s stellar year. Moderator Ray Subers, head of film at NRG, presented Blum and Wan with a stat that theater attendance for horror films in 2026 went up 7% from pre-pandemic levels, while attendance for all other genre films (action, sci-fi, rom-coms) decreased. Blum theorized this was because watching horror on the big screen is “participatory,” and that audiences craved a “collective experience” after emerging from COVID lockdown.

“I think that after COVID, audiences ran back to sporting events and ran back to concerts, but they had been fed movies,” Blum said. “Kids had been fed movies so much at home that it took longer to discover and remember the movies [in the theater]. And I think horror specifically, if there’s any genre that’s close to a concert or a sporting event, I think horror is more than anything else because it’s so participatory. I think movies generally, but horror specifically, are kind of joining sports and concerts as a great way to get out of your house and have a collective, fun, exciting thing to do that doesn’t involve your phone.”

The conversation then shifted to “Obsession.” Blum joined as an executive producer shortly after Focus Features acquired the film, which, from a budget of less than $1 million, grossed over $500 million worldwide. Blum said he thinks “Obsession” took off for two reasons. The first is because young people can relate to the “universal feeling” of being “obsessed or having someone obsessed with them.” The second reason was that directorCurry Barkersharpened his filmmaking skills on YouTube and social media before coming to Hollywood.

“I think that he has a dialogue with his audience, which he has honed over years and years and years of putting little pieces of content on YouTube and watching his audience react and adjusting to it,” Blum said. “The best way I can describe it is it almost feels like when you’re watching the movie, Curry is like whispering in your ear little funny things or like you’re talking to this invisible hand that’s directing the movie in a way that’s very unique.”

Wan added that the success of “Obsession” has inspired a whole new generation of filmmakers wanting to make scary movies, which reminds him of when he was trying to break into the industry with “Saw.”

“That stigma is gone. Horror has crossed over from the black sheep of the household, right?” Wan said. “I really do credit the younger generation with accepting the genre in a big way and not turning your nose down on it in a snooty way. When I was doing ‘Saw’ people looked down on it, right? And it was only a certain demographic that would come out and support the films that we made. But today, like today, it is cool and hip to be making horror films.”
title_zh: 傑森·布拉姆(Jason Blum)和詹姆斯·溫(James Wan)討論為什麼恐怖片是好萊塢最熱門的類型，以及《迷戀》(Obsession)如何在布拉姆豪斯原子影業(Blumhouse Atomic)的《恐懼的商業》中取得成功。
content_zh:
由Jack Dunn報導

布倫哈姆斯(Blumhouse)的執行長傑森·布倫(Jason Blum)和詹姆斯·溫(James Wan)在他們的「恐懼商業」(Business of Fear)座談會上於週三進行了一次勝利的巡演，討論了恐怖片在票房上的輝煌一年，以及為何《著迷》(Obsession)成為夏季的突破性熱門影片。

但在開始討論恐怖話題之前，他們必須先談及名稱變更。布倫哈姆斯和溫的原子怪獸(Atomic Monster)在2024年合併，因此合併後的品牌被稱為布倫哈姆斯原子怪獸(Blumhouse Atomic Monster)。最近，在11月初，布倫哈姆斯原子怪獸重新品牌化為僅僅是布倫哈姆斯原子(Blumhouse Atomic)。布倫解釋說，他們重新品牌化是為了給兩家公司之間的整體品牌提供更明確的身份，同時也為兩個獨特的品牌清理了空間，以便能夠為他們的作品獲得應有的認可。

溫補充說，布倫哈姆斯原子怪獸的名稱也「有點冗長」。

「正如傑森所指出的，這仍然是布倫哈姆斯的電影和原子怪獸的電影，」溫補充道。「我們仍然作為一家公司製作電影，但仍然在兩個品牌之下。我們推出了一系列電影，因此我們必須進行某種劃分。有些電影在原子怪獸那裡更受歡迎，有些電影在布倫哈姆斯那裡更受歡迎。在電影的開頭，儘管會顯示布倫哈姆斯原子呈現(Blumhouse Atomic Presents)，我們的標誌仍然會單獨出現。」

接著談到了恐怖片的卓越年份。主持人雷·蘇伯斯(Ray Subers)，NRG的電影部門負責人，向布倫和溫提供了一個統計數據，顯示2026年恐怖片的觀影人數比疫情前增長了7%，而其他類型電影（動作片、科幻片、浪漫喜劇）的觀影人數則減少。布倫推測這是因為在大銀幕上觀看恐怖片是「參與式的」，觀眾在經歷COVID封鎖後渴望「集體體驗」。

「我認為在COVID之後，觀眾回到了體育賽事和音樂會，但他們在家裡已經看了很多電影，」布倫說。「孩子們在家裡看了這麼多電影，以至於他們需要更長的時間來發現和記住在電影院的電影。我認為恐怖片特別如此，如果有任何類型的電影接近音樂會或體育賽事，我認為恐怖片是最接近的，因為它是如此參與式。我認為一般的電影，尤其是恐怖片，正與體育和音樂會一起成為一種很好的方式，讓人們走出家門，參加一個集體的、有趣的、刺激的活動，而不需要使用手機。」

隨後，對話轉向了《著迷》。布倫在焦點影業(Focus Features)收購該片後不久便加入擔任執行製片人，該片以不到100萬美元的預算，全球票房超過5億美元。布倫表示，他認為《著迷》之所以成功有兩個原因。第一是因為年輕人能夠與「被著迷或對某人著迷的普遍感受」產生共鳴。第二個原因是導演庫里·巴克(Curry Barker)在進入好萊塢之前，在YouTube和社交媒體上磨練了他的電影製作技巧。

“我認為他與觀眾之間有著對話，這是他多年來在YouTube上發布小片段並觀察觀眾反應後磨練出來的，”布倫(Blum)說。“我能形容的最好方式是，當你在看這部電影時，庫里(Curry)就像在你耳邊低語一些有趣的事情，或者你就像在與這隻看不見的手對話，這隻手以一種非常獨特的方式引導著電影。”

溫(Wan)補充說，《著迷》(Obsession)的成功激勵了一整代新的電影製作人想要拍攝恐怖片，這讓他想起了自己當初試圖進入這個行業時拍攝《驚魂記》(Saw)的情景。

“那種污名已經消失了。恐怖片已經不再是家中的黑羊了，對吧？”溫說。“我真的要感謝年輕一代以大方的態度接受這個類型，而不是以傲慢的方式嗤之以鼻。當我在拍攝《驚魂記》時，人們對它嗤之以鼻，對吧？而且只有特定的人群會出來支持我們製作的電影。但今天，像今天這樣，拍攝恐怖片已經變得酷炫和時尚。”
